details.label: Summary
details.text: An isolated damaging wind threat may persist in the remaining valid portion of the watch area through 18Z. Additional severe storms appear possible this afternoon across parts of central into southeast Illinois, potentially requiring a new watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Elevated thunderstorms forming atop of the morning MCS cold pool have gradually consolidated into a cluster over portions of Knox, Stark, and Peoria Counties in west-central IL as of 1705Z with some earlier velocity enhancement noted in KDVN radar data. Given the presence of fairly substantial convective inhibition for surface-based parcels, it remains uncertain whether a cold pool can organize with that convection, which would signal some increase in damaging wind potential. Additional severe storms appear possible this afternoon along the leading edge of the MCS gust front over central IL, where filtered sunshine has allowed temperatures to warm into the mid 80s with MLCAPE estimated in the 2000-3000 J/kg range, per latest objective analysis. Should that scenario unfold, a new severe thunderstorm watch would need to be considered for portions of central into southeast IL

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms will pose an isolated risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts this afternoon from the Niagra Frontier into the Northern Tier of PA

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms will pose an isolated risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts this afternoon from the Niagra Frontier into the Northern Tier of PA

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms are ongoing across southern Ontario and portions of the Niagra Frontier as of 1710 UTC, with this activity forecast to develop southeastward into southern NY/northern PA through this afternoon. While surface temperatures remain seasonably cool in the low-to-mid 70s F, surface dewpoints in the low-to-mid 60s F and regionally steep mid-level lapse rates of 6-7 C/km are supporting modest buoyancy, with 1000 to locally 1500 J/kg MLCAPE indicated by recent objective analysis. Concurrently, a mid/upper-level speed max will continue to shift eastward from Lower Michigan into NY/PA through this afternoon and evening. This enhanced mid/upper flow (sampled by the BUF VAD profile and the 12 UTC BUF observed sounding) will continue to promote effective shear of 30-40 kts and elongated hodographs favorable for supercell structures. The primary risks associated with this activity will be large hail and damaging wind gusts. Current expectations are for convective coverage and the severe risk to remain too isolated for watch issuance; however, a targeted Severe Thunderstorm Watch could be considered should greater storm/severe coverage prevail

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Forcing for ascent within the southwest flank of an MCV moving through the lower Savannah River Valley will combine with broadly confluent low-level flow to yield scattered thunderstorms this afternoon. Area VWPs indicate relatively weak vertical shear across the region, which will limit the potential for storm organization. However, the 12Z JAX sounding sampled the presence of a very moist and strongly unstable air mass with MLCAPE of 3000-3500 J/kg. As such, the potential will exist for locally intense wet microbursts capable of a few damaging wind gusts, especially if storms can merge into clusters
